title: A Short History Of The Minimum Wage
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的 English Learning for Curious Minds。在这里，你可以一边听引人入胜的故事，了解世界上各种奇妙有趣的事物，一边提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊最低工资。

sentences.en: In many countries around the world, there are laws stating the minimum amount of money that an employee should earn for doing a job, the so-called “minimum wage”.
sentences.zh: 在世界上的许多国家，都有法律规定雇员从事某项工作应获得的最低报酬，即所谓的“最低工资”。

sentences.en: To some, this is a worthy achievement, a law that protects workers from exploitation at the hands of greedy corporations.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这是一项了不起的成就，是一部保护工人免受贪婪公司剥削的法律。

sentences.en: To others, it is a red herring, a feel-good measure that hurts the very people it aims to help.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，这是一种误导，是一项自我感觉良好但实际上伤害了它本想帮助的人的措施。

sentences.en: So, in this episode, we’ll explore the history of the minimum wage, we’ll look at some of the arguments for and against, we’ll look at some examples of countries where it has worked, others where it hasn’t, we’ll talk about the particular case of the UK, and we’ll also learn about how sometimes not having a minimum wage, surprisingly enough, actually results in higher wages for the lowest paid workers.
sentences.zh: 所以，在本期节目中，我们将探讨最低工资的历史，看看支持和反对的观点，研究一些成功和失败的国家案例，讨论英国的特殊情况，我们还将了解到，令人惊讶的是，有时没有最低工资反而会让收入最低的工人拿到更高的薪水。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it, and talk about The Minimum Wage.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们进入正题，聊聊最低工资。

sentences.en: I imagine that many of you can remember your first real paycheck.
sentences.zh: 我想你们中的许多人还记得自己领到的第一份真正的薪水。

sentences.en: In the autumn, after I finished school, I worked in a pub in a nearby village, pulling pints, serving drinks and making small talk with the regulars.
sentences.zh: 在我毕业后的那个秋天，我在附近村庄的一家酒吧工作，负责打啤酒、端饮料，并和常客们闲聊。

sentences.en: The shifts were quite long at times. 12 pm to 12 am was the longest one, if I’m not mistaken.
sentences.zh: 有时班次很长。如果我没记错的话，最长的一班是从中午 12 点到凌晨 12 点。

sentences.en: Afterwards, I would go home on my bike, exhausted after 12 hours on my feet, serving drinkers who would sometimes get increasingly troublesome as the night went on.
sentences.zh: 之后，我会骑自行车回家，站了 12 个小时后精疲力竭，还要招待那些随着夜色渐深有时会变得越来越难缠的酒客。

sentences.en: For my work, I was paid £4.25 every hour - the minimum wage in the UK at the time, or at least, the minimum wage for everyone under the age of 22.
sentences.zh: 我的报酬是每小时 4.25 英镑——这是当时英国的最低工资，或者至少是 22 岁以下人群的最低工资。

sentences.en: And for reference, this was in 2005, so it was about €6.
sentences.zh: 供参考，那是 2005 年，所以大约是 6 欧元。

sentences.en: It seemed like a lot to me. But I was living at home with my parents, I didn’t pay rent, and I didn’t pay for groceries.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这似乎很多。但我当时和父母住在一起，不用付房租，也不用买菜。

sentences.en: It seemed like a lot to a fresh-faced 18-year-old, but clearly, it wasn’t, at least not in the UK.
sentences.zh: 对于一个稚气未脱的 18 岁少年来说，这似乎很多，但显然事实并非如此，至少在英国不是。

sentences.en: It was the minimum that any company was legally allowed to pay an employee; I literally couldn’t have been paid any less.
sentences.zh: 这是法律允许公司支付给员工的最低报酬；我真的不可能拿到更少的钱了。

sentences.en: But of course, this idea, that the government should step in and set a legal minimum for how little someone can be paid, is a relatively new concept.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这种政府应该介入并为薪酬设定法定最低限额的想法，是一个相对较新的概念。

sentences.en: For most of history, wages were determined by the market, or more accurately, by power.
sentences.zh: 在历史的大部分时间里，工资是由市场决定的，或者更准确地说，是由权力决定的。

sentences.en: Whether you worked in the fields or later on in a factory, the amount you were paid was the result of a direct agreement between you and your employer.
sentences.zh: 无论你是在田间劳作，还是后来在工厂做工，你拿到的报酬都是你和雇主直接协商的结果。

sentences.en: If you were desperate for work, and your employer knew it, they could pay you next to nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果你急需工作，而你的雇主又知道这一点，他们可以付给你极低的报酬。

sentences.en: And they often did. Pick up any Charles Dickens novel and you’ll find depictions of evil employers squeezing their workers for every last penny, paying them the absolute minimum possible for them to not die of starvation or from freezing to death at home.
sentences.zh: 他们也经常这么做。随便翻开一本 Charles Dickens 的小说，你都能看到对邪恶雇主的描写，他们榨干工人的每一分钱，只支付给他们勉强维持生命、不至于饿死或冻死在家里的最低报酬。

sentences.en: And of course, the UK was not alone in this, in its basically “zero state intervention” policy in terms of the amount an employer needed to pay its employees.
sentences.zh: 当然，在雇主支付给员工报酬方面，英国并不是唯一实行这种基本上“零国家干预”政策的国家。

sentences.en: All over the world, workers typically had few protections, few safeguards ensuring that they were paid enough to live a decent life.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，工人通常几乎没有保护，也没有保障能确保他们获得足以过上体面生活的报酬。

sentences.en: And although it is now popular to talk about how we must crush the rich and how evil billionaires are exploiting the poor, the reality is that living standards and disposable income for the poorest in society, in practically every country in the world, have never been higher than they are today.
sentences.zh: 虽然现在流行谈论我们必须打倒富人，以及邪恶的亿万富翁如何剥削穷人，但现实是，在世界上几乎每一个国家，社会最底层人群的生活水平和可支配收入从未像今天这样高。

sentences.en: This is thanks to economic growth, but there is an argument to be made that it is also thanks to the concept of the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于经济增长，但也有观点认为，这也要归功于最低工资的概念。

sentences.en: In other words, the lowest salaries in society are higher than ever before, thanks to government intervention, laws protecting workers from low pay.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，由于政府的干预和保护工人免受低薪待遇的法律，社会最低工资比以往任何时候都要高。

sentences.en: Governments first started to get involved at the end of the 19th century, and in fact, the first countries to legislate minimum wage laws were in a part of the world you might not necessarily expect: not post-revolutionary France or English factory workers weary of working 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.
sentences.zh: 政府在 19 世纪末开始介入，事实上，最早制定最低工资法的国家可能出乎你的意料：不是革命后的法国，也不是那些厌倦了每周 7 天、每天工作 12 小时的英国工厂工人。

sentences.en: It was, in fact, on the other side of the world, in Australia and New Zealand.
sentences.zh: 事实上，是在地球的另一端，澳大利亚和新西兰。

sentences.en: In both countries, there was growing concern that certain workers in certain industries, especially women working in clothes factories, were being paid so little that they couldn’t afford even the basic necessities of life.
sentences.zh: 在这两个国家，人们越来越担心某些行业的某些工人，特别是服装厂的女工，拿到的报酬太少，甚至无法负担基本的生活必需品。

sentences.en: A small number of employers held all the power, and governments feared that unless something changed, there would be civil unrest, and they would have a French Revolution-type situation on their hands, with angry workers rising up against their rulers.
sentences.zh: 少数雇主掌握了所有权力，政府担心除非做出改变，否则会出现社会动荡，他们将面临类似法国大革命的局面，愤怒的工人会起来反抗统治者。

sentences.en: The first laws came into place in 1894 in New Zealand, and in Australia two years later.
sentences.zh: 第一批法律于 1894 年在新西兰实施，两年后在澳大利亚实施。

sentences.en: Initially, they were focused on individual industries, but they quickly spread.
sentences.zh: 最初，这些法律针对的是个别行业，但很快就普及开来。

sentences.en: The idea was codified by a 1907 law called The Harvester Case, which stated that there should be a 'living wage' for, and I’m quoting directly, a man, his wife, and three children to "live in frugal comfort".
sentences.zh: 这一理念被 1907 年一项名为“哈维斯特案”（The Harvester Case）的法律所确立，该法律规定，应该为一名男子、他的妻子和三个孩子提供“生活工资”，我直接引用原文，以使他们能“过上简朴舒适的生活”。

sentences.en: Frugal, by the way, means careful with money, so frugal comfort means living comfortably but without any luxuries.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，frugal 的意思是省钱，所以“简朴舒适”意味着生活舒适但没有任何奢侈品。

sentences.en: In other words, every job should pay enough to support a decent life for a family of five: a man, his wife, and three children.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，每一份工作都应该支付足够的报酬，以维持一个五口之家（一名男子、他的妻子和三个孩子）的体面生活。

sentences.en: Now, perhaps you can complain about this seeming like an archaic view of the world, of a man going out to earn a living while his wife and three children stay at home.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会抱怨这看起来像是一种过时的世界观，即男人外出挣钱养家，而妻子和三个孩子留在家里。

sentences.en: This was more than 100 years ago, so clearly, certain things were different.
sentences.zh: 这是 100 多年前的事了，所以显然某些情况是不同的。

sentences.en: But what you might also quite rightly point out is that this “living wage” must surely have been more generous than a modern “living wage”, given that it aims to support one non-working parent and three children.
sentences.zh: 但你可能也会很正确地指出，这种“生活工资”肯定比现代的“生活工资”更慷慨，因为它旨在供养一名不工作的家长和三个孩子。

sentences.en: In 21st-century Britain, at least, you would certainly struggle to support a family of five on the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 至少在 21 世纪的英国，你肯定很难靠最低工资供养一个五口之家。

sentences.en: But back to the start of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 回到 20 世纪初。

sentences.en: Understandably, the introduction of the minimum wage proved popular with workers, and the idea quickly spread.
sentences.zh: 可以理解的是，最低工资的引入受到了工人们的欢迎，这一理念迅速传播开来。

sentences.en: In 1909, the United Kingdom passed something called the Trade Boards Act, which established wage boards to set minimum wages in industries that were considered especially exploitative, things like garment work, where mainly women and children were exploited, forced to work long hours in terrible conditions for very low pay.
sentences.zh: 1909 年，英国通过了《贸易委员会法》（Trade Boards Act），设立了工资委员会，为那些被认为剥削特别严重的行业设定最低工资，比如服装业，那里主要是妇女和儿童受到剥削，被迫在恶劣的条件下长时间工作，报酬却极低。

sentences.en: In the United States, a national minimum wage came a little later, but not without a fight.
sentences.zh: 在美国，全国最低工资出现得稍晚一些，而且并非一帆风顺。

sentences.en: It was introduced in 1938, during the Great Depression, as part of President Franklin D.
sentences.zh: 它于 1938 年大萧条期间作为 Franklin D. Roosevelt 总统“新政”的一部分被引入。

sentences.en: Roosevelt’s New Deal. At the time, it was set at $0.25 an hour, around $5.70 in inflation-adjusted terms.
sentences.zh: 当时，它被设定为每小时 0.25 美元，按通货膨胀调整后约为 5.70 美元。

sentences.en: Even though the idea had spread through much of Europe, it was still a radical idea in America.
sentences.zh: 尽管这一理念已经传遍了欧洲大部分地区，但在美国仍然是一个激进的想法。

sentences.en: It was the biggest economy in the world, the roaring heart of capitalism, and the idea that the government should intervene and say “this is the minimum a company can pay its employees”, well, that was controversial.
sentences.zh: 美国是世界上最大的经济体，是资本主义蓬勃发展的心脏，而政府应该介入并规定“这是公司支付给员工的最低限额”这种想法，嗯，那是很有争议的。

sentences.en: It would cost jobs, employers cried, it would result in people being paid less because companies would sack them.
sentences.zh: 雇主们大喊，这会减少就业机会，会导致人们拿到的钱更少，因为公司会解雇他们。

sentences.en: Companies would go out of business if they had to pay these higher wages.
sentences.zh: 如果必须支付这些更高的工资，公司就会倒闭。

sentences.en: To this, President Franklin D. Roosevelt had a plain answer: tough luck.
sentences.zh: 对此，Franklin D. Roosevelt 总统给出了一个直截了当的回答：算你们倒霉。

sentences.en: Or, as he put it, “it seems to me to be equally plain that no business, which depends for existence on paying less than living wages to its workers, has any right to continue in this country."
sentences.zh: 或者正如他所说，“在我看来，同样显而易见的是，任何依赖支付低于生活工资的报酬给工人才得以生存的企业，都没有权利在这个国家继续经营。”

sentences.en: In other words, if you can’t pay a fair wage to your employees, you deserve to go out of business.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你不能给员工支付合理的工资，你就活该倒闭。

sentences.en: Now, the minimum wage in the US today has not moved on much; the federal minimum wage is dismally low, at $7.25 an hour, but various states have different laws about what companies are required to pay their employees.
sentences.zh: 如今，美国的最低工资并没有太大进展；联邦最低工资低得可怜，为每小时 7.25 美元，但各州对于公司必须支付给员工的报酬有不同的法律规定。

sentences.en: Almost 100 years later, in the spiritual home of free-market capitalism, the debate about the minimum wage rages on.
sentences.zh: 近 100 年后，在这个自由市场资本主义的精神家园，关于最低工资的辩论仍在激烈进行。

sentences.en: As it does, in fact, in every country that has legislated on the minimum wage, or where there are talks about changing or increasing it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在每一个制定了最低工资法，或者正在讨论修改或提高最低工资的国家，情况都是如此。

sentences.en: Its supporters argue that it needs to be protected at all costs, created if it doesn’t exist already, or increased if it is considered too low.
sentences.zh: 支持者认为，必须不惜一切代价保护最低工资，如果没有就制定，如果认为太低就提高。

sentences.en: Without a fair minimum wage, the most vulnerable in society risk being even more exploited by powerful corporations.
sentences.zh: 如果没有合理的最低工资，社会中最弱势的群体就有可能受到强大公司更严重的剥削。

sentences.en: People would be at the mercy of employers who could pay as little as they liked, especially in industries where workers have very little bargaining power.
sentences.zh: 人们将任由雇主摆布，雇主想付多少就付多少，尤其是在工人几乎没有议价能力的行业。

sentences.en: A minimum wage ensures that there is at least a basic level of fairness, that no one working full-time should live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 最低工资确保了至少有基本的公平，即任何全职工作的人都不应该生活在贫困中。

sentences.en: On the other hand, critics argue that setting a minimum wage could actually harm the very people it is designed to help.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，批评者认为，设定最低工资实际上可能会伤害到它本想帮助的人。

sentences.en: If you set the minimum wage too high, they argue, employers might respond by hiring fewer people, cutting hours, replacing workers with machines, or, of course, with AI.
sentences.zh: 他们辩称，如果最低工资定得太高，雇主可能会通过减少招聘、缩短工时、用机器或者人工智能来取代工人作为回应。

sentences.en: They say that it can lead to higher unemployment, especially among young people, those with lower levels of education, or those entering the job market for the first time.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这会导致失业率上升，尤其是年轻人、受教育程度较低的人或初次进入职场的人。

sentences.en: In other words, some people might be better off, those who keep their jobs and their same hours, but others will lose their jobs completely and be in a much worse economic position.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，有些人可能会过得更好，即那些保住了工作且工时不变的人，但其他人将彻底失业，经济状况会变得糟糕得多。

sentences.en: And the arguments for and against the minimum wage go beyond ideas about how much money a worker will be paid.
sentences.zh: 关于最低工资的支持和反对观点，已经超出了工人能拿到多少钱的范畴。

sentences.en: On the “pro minimum wage” side, supporters argue that it can also boost morale and productivity.
sentences.zh: 在“支持最低工资”的一方，支持者认为这还能提高士气和生产力。

sentences.en: When workers feel they are being treated fairly and paid a decent wage, they are more likely to take pride in their work, stay with their employer for longer, and to contribute more.
sentences.zh: 当工人感到自己受到公平对待并获得体面的报酬时，他们更有可能为自己的工作感到自豪，在雇主那里待得更久，并做出更多贡献。

sentences.en: This is good for them, good for their mental health, and it’s also good for the business, because it reduces turnover and increases productivity.
sentences.zh: 这对他们有好处，对他们的心理健康有好处，对企业也有好处，因为它降低了员工流失率并提高了生产力。

sentences.en: Another argument in favour of the minimum wage is that it increases consumer spending.
sentences.zh: 另一个支持最低工资的论点是它能增加消费支出。

sentences.en: If low-wage workers have more money in their pockets, they are likely to spend it in their local communities, which helps stimulate the economy.
sentences.zh: 如果低收入工人兜里有更多的钱，他们很可能会在当地社区消费，这有助于刺激经济。

sentences.en: The wealthier an individual is, the higher proportion of their income they save, so if a company pays low earners more, they will typically spend a greater percentage of what they make than what the wealthy company owners would spend.
sentences.zh: 一个人越富有，他们储蓄的收入比例就越高，所以如果一家公司给低收入者支付更多报酬，他们通常会比富有的公司所有者花掉更大比例的收入。

sentences.en: So, it’s a good thing for local and general economic growth.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对当地和整体经济增长都是一件好事。

sentences.en: But there are also more arguments on the “anti-minimum wage” side.
sentences.zh: 但“反对最低工资”的一方也有更多论点。

sentences.en: Firstly, the concern that it puts pressure on small businesses.
sentences.zh: 首先，担心这会给小企业带来压力。

sentences.en: A large multinational company might be able to absorb the higher wage costs, but for a small shop or restaurant operating on wafer-thin profit margins, it could mean the difference between staying open or shutting down.
sentences.zh: 一家大型跨国公司也许能够承担更高的工资成本，但对于一家利润微薄的小商店或餐馆来说，这可能意味着继续营业或倒闭的区别。

sentences.en: Some economists argue that a blanket minimum wage is a blunt tool, like trying to tend to a flowerbed with a lawnmower instead of precise little scissors.
sentences.zh: 一些经济学家认为，一刀切的最低工资是一种笨拙的工具，就像试图用割草机而不是精细的小剪刀来打理花坛一样。

sentences.en: A blanket minimum wage treats every region and every industry the same, even though the cost of living and average wages vary hugely.
sentences.zh: 一刀切的最低工资对每个地区和每个行业都一视同仁，尽管生活成本和平均工资差异巨大。

sentences.en: In the UK, for example, the entire country is treated in the same way, it is a national minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 例如，在英国，全国都以同样的方式对待，实行的是全国最低工资。

sentences.en: As of April this year, it’s £12.21 an hour whether you live in central London or a remote village in the north of the country.
sentences.zh: 截至今年 4 月，无论你住在伦敦市中心还是该国北部偏远的村庄，最低工资都是每小时 12.21 英镑。

sentences.en: And to state the obvious, like in almost every country, the cost of living varies a lot.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，就像几乎每个国家一样，生活成本差异很大。

sentences.en: What you can buy with £12.21 in London is very different from what you can buy with £12.21 in rural Wales or even a lower-cost-of-living city like Belfast or Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦用 12.21 英镑能买到的东西，与在威尔士农村，甚至是在贝尔法斯特或纽卡斯尔这样生活成本较低的城市能买到的东西大不相同。

sentences.en: Yet the pay for a minimum wage worker is the same.
sentences.zh: 然而，最低工资工人的报酬却是相同的。

sentences.en: This isn’t fair for workers, the argument goes, someone in London needs to be paid more, and someone in Newcastle doesn’t need to be paid as much.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，这对工人不公平，伦敦的人需要更高的报酬，而纽卡斯尔的人不需要那么多。

sentences.en: It also isn’t fair for businesses. A wage that is perfectly reasonable in high-cost central London might be completely unaffordable for a small business in a rural town.
sentences.zh: 这对企业也不公平。在成本高昂的伦敦市中心完全合理的工资，对于农村小镇的一家小企业来说可能完全负担不起。

sentences.en: Now, I should add that some countries do legislate on the minimum wage at a more regional level, which evens out some of these disparities.
sentences.zh: 现在，我应该补充一点，有些国家确实在更具地区性的层面上制定最低工资法，这平衡了其中的一些差异。

sentences.en: In China, for example, the minimum wage in Beijing is almost 70% higher than it is in rural western China, which helps account for the different cost of living.
sentences.zh: 例如，在中国，北京的最低工资比中国西部农村高出近 70%，这有助于解释不同的生活成本。

sentences.en: There is also the argument that the minimum wage, if set too low, legitimises and encourages low pay.
sentences.zh: 还有一种观点认为，如果最低工资定得太低，就会使低薪合法化并鼓励低薪。

sentences.en: In the UK, many minimum wage workers are still forced to turn to the state for financial assistance.
sentences.zh: 在英国，许多拿最低工资的工人仍被迫向国家寻求经济援助。

sentences.en: But because their employers have met their legal obligations, they can wash their hands of the situation, saying “we’re paying what we need to do”, rather than paying a fair and honest wage to their workers.
sentences.zh: 但由于雇主已经履行了法律义务，他们就可以对这种情况撒手不管，说“我们已经支付了该付的钱”，而不是向工人支付公平诚实的工资。

sentences.en: And finally, there is also the argument that it does not necessarily target those who need help the most.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有一种观点认为，它不一定针对那些最需要帮助的人。

sentences.en: In some cases, the person earning a minimum wage might be a student living at home, like I was, or a second earner in a well-off household.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，赚取最低工资的人可能是像我当时那样住在家里的学生，或者是富裕家庭中的第二个收入来源者。

sentences.en: In other words, not everyone earning the minimum wage is living in poverty, and not everyone in poverty is earning the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，并非每个拿最低工资的人都生活在贫困中，也并非每个贫困人口都拿着最低工资。

sentences.en: So, what would happen if there were no minimum wage?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果没有最低工资会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: In theory, to the critics of the minimum wage at least, businesses and employees would be free to set their own wages.
sentences.zh: 理论上，至少对最低工资的批评者来说，企业和员工可以自由设定自己的工资。

sentences.en: People in high-cost-of-living areas would be paid more, and people in lower-cost-of-living areas would be paid less.
sentences.zh: 生活成本高地区的人报酬会更高，生活成本低地区的人报酬会更低。

sentences.en: And this is not just theory. There are actually plenty of examples of countries without minimum wage laws, some where employees are paid much more than in countries which have minimum wages.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是理论。实际上有很多没有最低工资法的国家案例，其中一些国家的员工报酬比有最低工资的国家要高得多。

sentences.en: Sweden, for example, has no minimum wage laws, yet it has one of the highest median wages in Europe.
sentences.zh: 例如，瑞典没有最低工资法，但它拥有欧洲最高的中位数工资之一。

sentences.en: In fact, most Scandinavian countries, which tend to be at the top of every table with average wages and living standards, they don’t have national minimum wage laws.
sentences.zh: 事实上，大多数斯堪的纳维亚国家在平均工资和生活水平方面往往名列前茅，但它们并没有全国性的最低工资法。

sentences.en: Now, this isn’t due to the great benevolence and kindness of Scandinavian employers, but rather that most jobs are covered by trade union agreements, so the union will negotiate wages on behalf of employees.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为斯堪的纳维亚雇主多么仁慈和善良，而是因为大多数工作都受工会协议保护，所以工会会代表员工协商工资。

sentences.en: These employees are highly protected in terms of what a company can pay them, the protection just comes from the trade union, not the state.
sentences.zh: 这些员工在公司支付报酬方面受到高度保护，只是这种保护来自工会，而不是国家。

sentences.en: The logic behind this is that wages are better determined by those who understand the specific needs of an industry, rather than by politicians, and, given the relatively high wages of the lowest-paid workers in Scandinavia, it’s hard to deny that it works pretty well.
sentences.zh: 这背后的逻辑是，工资最好由了解行业具体需求的人来决定，而不是由政治家决定。考虑到斯堪的纳维亚收入最低工人的工资相对较高，很难否认这种模式运作得非常好。

sentences.en: Now, the last thing I want to talk about today is the situation in the UK, because something interesting has been happening with the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 现在，我今天最后想谈的是英国的情况，因为最低工资方面发生了一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Ever since the national minimum wage was introduced by Tony Blair in 1999, it has continued to rise.
sentences.zh: 自从 Tony Blair 在 1999 年引入全国最低工资以来，它一直在持续上涨。

sentences.en: It started at £3.60 an hour, and in April this year it was increased from £11.44 to £12.21 an hour.
sentences.zh: 它起步时为每小时 3.60 英镑，今年 4 月从每小时 11.44 英镑增加到了 12.21 英镑。

sentences.en: Compounded, this is an average growth of almost 5% a year, which is significantly higher than the growth in non-minimum wage jobs, which increased at a rate of 2.8% a year.
sentences.zh: 复合计算，这相当于每年近 5% 的平均增长，明显高于非最低工资工作的增长，后者的增长率为每年 2.8%。

sentences.en: So the minimum wage increased almost twice as much as the average salary, which has led to this slightly unusual situation in which the difference between minimum wage jobs and more skilled jobs has been massively reduced.
sentences.zh: 因此，最低工资的增幅几乎是平均工资的两倍，这导致了一种略显反常的情况，即最低工资工作与高技能工作之间的差距被大幅缩小了。

sentences.en: For example, the salary for a graduate nuclear engineer in the UK starts at around £22,000 year, which is around €25,000.
sentences.zh: 例如，英国核工程专业毕业生的起薪约为每年 22,000 英镑，约合 25,000 欧元。

sentences.en: The minimum wage of £12.21 an hour, for someone working full-time, would result in a salary of £23,873 a year, more than a graduate nuclear engineer.
sentences.zh: 而对于一个全职工作的人来说，每小时 12.21 英镑的最低工资将导致年薪达到 23,873 英镑，比核工程专业毕业生还要高。

sentences.en: Now, clearly, the nuclear engineer most likely has better career prospects; they can get promoted, paid more, and perhaps the work is more fulfilling than in many minimum-wage jobs.
sentences.zh: 显然，核工程师很可能拥有更好的职业前景；他们可以获得晋升，拿到更高的薪水，而且工作可能比许多最低工资的工作更有成就感。

sentences.en: Perhaps you might even argue that this is the way it should be, that someone doing public service cleaning the streets in the rain should be paid just as much, more, even, than someone sitting behind a desk and answering emails.
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至会认为本该如此，即一个在雨中清理街道从事公共服务的人，拿到的报酬应该和坐在办公桌后面回邮件的人一样多，甚至更多。

sentences.en: But there have been plenty of stories in the British press over the past few years of young people complaining about this situation, asking themselves why they should slave away at university for 3 or 4 years, getting into tens of thousands of pounds of debt only to get a job where they are paid the same as someone working in an unskilled, minimum wage job.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，英国媒体上有大量关于年轻人抱怨这种状况的报道，他们自问为什么要辛苦读三四年大学，背负数万英镑的债务，结果却只能找到一份报酬和非技术性最低工资工作一样的工作。

sentences.en: “What’s the point of studying and working hard,” they ask, “if it isn’t going to result in any better financial situation?”
sentences.zh: 他们问道：“如果努力学习和工作不能带来更好的经济状况，那还有什么意义呢？”

sentences.en: To wrap things up, the minimum wage is one of those fascinating topics that divides people on both sides of the political spectrum.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，最低工资是那些让不同政治派别的人产生分歧的迷人话题之一。

sentences.en: On the right, there are those who oppose it because they see it as excessive government intervention in the free market, something that distorts natural supply and demand and risks killing jobs.
sentences.zh: 在右翼，有人反对它，因为他们认为这是政府对自由市场的过度干预，扭曲了自然的供求关系，并有减少就业机会的风险。

sentences.en: But there are also those on the right who support it as a way of reducing the need for government welfare, arguing that if people are paid more, they rely less on the state.
sentences.zh: 但右翼中也有人支持它，认为这可以减少对政府福利的需求，理由是如果人们拿到的报酬更多，他们对国家的依赖就会减少。

sentences.en: On the left, there are those who support it because it protects vulnerable workers, reduces inequality, and ensures a basic level of dignity in work.
sentences.zh: 在左翼，有人支持它，因为它保护了弱势工人，减少了不平等，并确保了工作的基本尊严。

sentences.en: But they have colleagues on the left who criticise it as a distraction, arguing that it doesn't go far enough, and that we should be talking instead about living wages, stronger unions, or even universal basic income.
sentences.zh: 但左翼中也有同事批评这是一种干扰，认为这做得还不够，我们应该讨论生活工资、更强大的工会，甚至是全民基本收入。

sentences.en: Indeed, when I was researching this episode and I wanted to double-check the date that Tony Blair’s government implemented the minimum wage, I googled “Tony Blair minimum wage”.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我为这期节目做调研，想再次确认 Tony Blair 政府实施最低工资的日期时，我谷歌搜索了“Tony Blair minimum wage”。

sentences.en: The first two results I got were both from left-leaning publications: Jacobin and The Guardian.
sentences.zh: 我得到的头两个结果都来自倾向左翼的刊物：《雅各宾》（Jacobin）和《卫报》（The Guardian）。

sentences.en: The first result read “Britain’s Minimum Wage Law Has Been an Abject Failure”.
sentences.zh: 第一个结果写着“英国的最低工资法是一次惨痛的失败”。

sentences.en: And the second read, “Minimum wage is UK’s ‘most successful economic policy in a generation’”.
sentences.zh: 第二个结果则写着“最低工资是英国‘一代人以来最成功的经济政策’”。

sentences.en: It just goes to show that when it comes to the minimum wage, two people who might otherwise agree on most things can look at exactly the same policy and come to drastically different conclusions.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明，在最低工资问题上，两个在大多数事情上可能达成一致的人，在面对完全相同的政策时，也可能得出截然不同的结论。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是今天关于最低工资的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 我希望这是一期有趣的节目，并且你学到了一些新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对本期节目的看法。

sentences.en: Is there a minimum wage in your country?
sentences.zh: 你们国家有最低工资标准吗？

sentences.en: How has it changed over time, and what do you think about its advantages and disadvantages?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它发生了怎样的变化？你如何看待它的优缺点？

sentences.en: For the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 对于会员朋友们，你们可以直接前往我们的社区论坛 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他求知欲强的朋友们交流。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的 English Learning for Curious Minds。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你平安，我们下期节目再见。
